title: Grammar: Advanced Counter-Argument Patterns in Philosophical Writing
grammarTip:
Сильное эссе включает КОНТРАРГУМЕНТ — это показывает интеллектуальную честность:

① ПРЕДСТАВЬ контраргумент:
"Admittedly, some argue that X..."
"It is true that X has certain advantages..."
"One could argue that X is the case..."

② ПРИЗНАЙ его частичную правоту:
"This is a valid point to some extent."
"There is some truth in this argument."

③ НО отвергни или ограничь его:
"However, this overlooks..."
"Nevertheless, the evidence suggests..."
"Yet this argument fails to consider..."

④ УСИЛЬ свою позицию:
"In fact, the evidence clearly shows..."
"Furthermore, research demonstrates..."

💡 Структура: Concession → Limitation → Your stronger argument

grammarTable.subject: Introducing an objection
grammarTable.verb: It might be objected that / One might argue that / A critic would say
grammarTable.example: "It might be objected that consequentialism ignores individual rights."

grammarTable.subject: Acknowledging merit
grammarTable.verb: This objection has force / There is some truth in / It is true that X
grammarTable.example: "This objection has genuine force — consequences clearly do matter."

grammarTable.subject: Limiting the concession
grammarTable.verb: however / yet / but / nevertheless + main counter
grammarTable.short: but the objection does not succeed because...
grammarTable.example: "However, the objection fails to establish that consequences are all that matters."

grammarTable.subject: Qualifying the position
grammarTable.verb: I do not claim X, but only Y / This is not to say X, but rather Y
grammarTable.example: "This is not to say that outcomes are irrelevant, but only that they cannot override all other considerations."

grammarTable.subject: Distinguishing cases
grammarTable.verb: in this case / in extreme cases / in ordinary situations
grammarTable.short: your claim holds in X context
grammarTable.example: "In ordinary moral situations, the rule holds. In extreme dilemmas, it may need to be qualified."

grammarTable.subject: Drawing a conclusion
grammarTable.verb: It follows that / We may conclude that / The upshot is
grammarTable.example: "It follows that deontological constraints cannot be entirely dismissed, even by consequentialists."

rows.form: "One might object that…" / "A critic could argue that…"
rows.example: "One might object that my argument proves too much — that it would justify conclusions I am not willing to accept."

rows.form: "It might be thought that…" / "It could be suggested that…"
rows.example: "It might be thought that this conflates two different senses of the term."

rows.form: "The strongest objection to this view is…"
rows.example: "The strongest objection to this view is that it renders many ordinary moral practices indefensible."

rows.form: "From a consequentialist / deontological / virtue perspective, one might argue…"
rows.example: "From a consequentialist perspective, one might argue that the ends justify the means in this case."

rows.form: "This objection has genuine force." / "The point is well taken."
rows.example: "This objection has genuine force — Kant's account does fail to capture certain aspects of moral experience."

rows.form: "It is true that X." / "I concede that X."
rows.example: "It is true that the argument, as stated, is vulnerable to this criticism."

rows.form: "To some extent, this is correct." / "There is something to this objection."
rows.example: "There is something to this criticism — the distinction I draw may be less clear than I initially suggested."

rows.form: "Admittedly, X. That said, Y."
rows.example: "Admittedly, care ethics cannot resolve all dilemmas. That said, it illuminates what the other frameworks miss."

rows.form: "However, this objection misses the point that…"
rows.example: "However, this objection misses the point that the case at issue is not a case of merely harming to benefit."

rows.form: "Nevertheless, the objection does not establish that X."
rows.example: "Nevertheless, the objection does not establish that the distinction is without moral significance."

rows.form: "The objection succeeds against a weaker version of my claim, but not against the stronger."
rows.example: "This objection succeeds against the crude version of the argument, but not against the more nuanced position I am defending."

rows.form: "Even granting this, the main argument still holds."
rows.example: "Even granting the force of this criticism, the overall case for care ethics remains compelling."

grammarExtra.title: Qualifying and Distinguishing: Limiting the Claim

rows.form: "I am not claiming X, but only that Y."
rows.example: "I am not claiming that consequences never matter, only that they cannot override all deontological constraints."

rows.form: "This is not to deny X, but to insist that Y."
rows.example: "This is not to deny that institutions matter, but to insist that individual character matters too."

rows.form: "In typical cases X holds. In exceptional cases, X may need qualification."
rows.example: "In ordinary moral situations, the principle of honesty is sound. In extreme dilemmas, it may conflict with other obligations."

rows.form: "My claim is the modest one that X, not the stronger claim that Y."
rows.example: "My claim is the modest one that relationships generate genuine obligations, not the stronger claim that these override all others."

rows.form: "It follows that…" / "We may therefore conclude…"
rows.example: "It follows that neither pure consequentialism nor pure deontology can give a fully adequate account of morality."

rows.form: "The upshot of this argument is…"
rows.example: "The upshot is that moral philosophy needs multiple frameworks, not a single master theory."

rows.form: "In light of the above…" / "On the basis of these considerations…"
rows.example: "In light of the above, it seems that care ethics adds something genuinely important to moral theory."

rows.form: "What this shows is that…" / "The lesson to draw is…"
rows.example: "What this shows is that moral intuitions should not be too quickly dismissed in favour of theoretical elegance."

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct phrase to introduce a counter-view.
exercises.text: "___ ___ that this argument proves too much, yielding conclusions no one accepts."
exercises.hint: "One might object that…" = introducing an opposing argument charitably

exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ the theory is vulnerable to this objection. ___ ___ ___, the central claim remains defensible." (acknowledge, then counter)
exercises.correct: It is true that / That said
exercises.hint: "It is true that X. That said, Y." = concede then counter

exercises.text: "This objection has force. ___, it does not establish that consequences are all that matters."
exercises.hint: "This objection has force. However, it does not establish X." = acknowledge then counter

exercises.text: "___ am not ___ that consequences are irrelevant, ___ only that they cannot override all deontological constraints."
exercises.hint: "I am not claiming X, but only Y" = limiting the claim precisely

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct phrase for drawing a conclusion after a counter-argument.
exercises.text: "___ ___ the above, neither pure consequentialism nor virtue ethics alone is fully adequate."
exercises.hint: "In light of the above" = drawing a conclusion based on what was discussed

exercises.instruction: Complete the phrase for introducing the strongest objection.
exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ objection to this view is that it renders ordinary moral practices indefensible."
exercises.hint: "The strongest objection to this view is…" = setting up the objection charitably

exercises.instruction: Choose the structure that best qualifies a claim.
exercises.text: "___ is not to say that character is irrelevant to action, but ___ to insist it is not the only factor."
exercises.hint: "This is not to say X, but rather to insist Y" = precise qualification

exercises.instruction: Complete the counter after conceding the point.
exercises.text: "Even ___ the force of this criticism, the overall case for care ethics remains persuasive."
exercises.hint: "Even granting X, Y still holds" = conceding then countering

exercises.instruction: Which sentence introduces an opposing view most charitably?
opts: "From a consequentialist perspective, one might argue that this distinction is merely semantic."
exercises.correct: "From a consequentialist perspective, one might argue that this distinction is merely semantic."
exercises.hint: "From X perspective, one might argue that…" = charitable introduction of opposing view

exercises.text: "___ ___ is that multiple ethical frameworks each capture something important, and none is complete on its own."
exercises.hint: "The upshot is that…" = the practical conclusion to draw

opts: "In ordinary cases, the principle holds; in extreme dilemmas, it may require qualification."
"The rule never applies in any situation."
exercises.correct: "In ordinary cases, the principle holds; in extreme dilemmas, it may require qualification."
exercises.hint: "In typical cases X; in exceptional cases, X may need qualification" = distinguishing cases

exercises.instruction: Complete the phrase "the point is well taken."
exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ ___ — the argument does commit to a strong claim. However, this is precisely what the argument needs to establish."
exercises.hint: "The point is well taken" = acknowledging validity of objection before countering

exercises.instruction: Choose the most academic way to introduce an objection.
opts: "It might be objected that this argument is circular."
exercises.correct: "It might be objected that this argument is circular."
exercises.hint: "It might be objected that…" = formal, academic introduction of counter-view

exercises.text: "My claim is the ___ ___ that relationships generate moral obligations, not the stronger claim that they override all other obligations."
exercises.hint: "My claim is the modest one that X, not the stronger claim that Y"

exercises.instruction: Which correctly concludes an argument after engaging with counter-views?
opts: "It follows that no ethical framework is entirely satisfactory, but each contributes something valuable."
exercises.correct: "It follows that no ethical framework is entirely satisfactory, but each contributes something valuable."
exercises.hint: "It follows that…" = logical conclusion after considering counter-arguments

exercises.instruction: What does "even granting this" signal in academic writing?
opts: The writer fully accepts the objection
The writer is about to introduce a new topic
The writer concedes a point temporarily to show the main argument still holds
The writer has no response to the objection
exercises.correct: The writer concedes a point temporarily to show the main argument still holds
exercises.hint: "Even granting this, X still holds" = concede + counter structure

questions.text: "___ ___ that my argument has counterintuitive implications." (introducing the objection)
questions.hint: "One might object that…" = introducing the opposing view charitably

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ the theory faces this objection. ___ ___, the central insight remains valid." (concede + counter)
questions.correct: It is true that / That said
questions.hint: "It is true that X. That said, Y." = concede then counter

questions.text: "This objection has genuine force. ___, it does not establish that deontological constraints are worthless."
questions.hint: "Nevertheless" = despite the force of the objection, the counter still holds

questions.text: "___ granting the objection's force, the main argument still stands." (concessive conditional — even if granting)
questions.hint: "Even granting X, Y still holds" = concede for argument's sake, then counter

questions.text: "I ___ claiming that character is everything — only that it matters alongside consequences."
questions.hint: "I am not claiming X, but only Y" = precise qualification of position

questions.text: "The upshot of this argument is…" introduces a conclusion.
questions.hint: "The upshot is…" = the practical conclusion or result of the argument

questions.text: "___ ___ the above, we can conclude that no single ethical framework is fully adequate."
questions.hint: "In light of the above" = drawing a conclusion based on the preceding argument

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ objection to care ethics is that partiality can shade into tribalism."
questions.hint: "The strongest objection to X is…" = introducing the counter-argument at its most powerful

questions.text: "In ordinary situations, the principle applies. ___ extreme cases, it may need qualification." (distinguishing)
questions.hint: "In ordinary cases X; in extreme cases Y" = distinguishing different contexts

questions.text: "___ is not to say that outcomes are irrelevant, but rather to insist that they are not the only consideration."
opts: Both A and B are correct
questions.correct: Both A and B are correct
questions.hint: "This is not to say X, but to insist Y" and "It is not to say X" — both are correct

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ — the argument does commit to a strong claim. Nevertheless, it is precisely what the case requires." (= I acknowledge the point)
questions.hint: "The point is well taken" = acknowledging validity of objection

questions.text: Which sentence best introduces an opposing view in a formal essay?
opts: "From a deontological perspective, one might argue that this conclusion violates fundamental duties."
questions.correct: "From a deontological perspective, one might argue that this conclusion violates fundamental duties."
questions.hint: "From X perspective, one might argue that…" = most formal, charitable introduction
